reviews.evidence: Ships a dynamic reasoning-effort slider skin with native-mode toggle, 24 visual anchors, unsupported-model hiding, a preview image, and explicit interaction behavior.
reviews.concern: README gives little task-oriented usage beyond toggling the skin and slider; compatibility is documented only for one DSH release candidate.

reviews.evidence: Documents shipped launcher, scheduled jobs, screen-aware replies, local screen and meeting memory, voice dictation, runtime switching, worktrees, review board, and computer control with numerous screenshots and GIFs.
reviews.concern: It is explicitly an early macOS Apple Silicon release, while troubleshooting and end-user failure recovery are comparatively light for its broad surface.

reviews.evidence: Ships a Windows Git Bash minimal preset with automatic shell discovery, idempotent installation, sandbox gating, timeout/background execution, output truncation, spill files, and diagnostics.
reviews.concern: The README has only a short two-step user flow and no concrete visual or command-output demonstration; each call starts a fresh shell and requires full access or approval escalation.

reviews.evidence: Ships phone-adapted remote DSH access through Quick Tunnel with one-time pairing, per-device sessions, revocation, HTTP/WebSocket authentication, optional GitHub identity, and update prompts; README includes mobile, security, and architecture visuals.
reviews.concern: Most detailed operating, compatibility, threat-model, and troubleshooting procedures are delegated to linked documents rather than shown directly in the README.

reviews.evidence: Documents an end-to-end shipped flow for IMAP collection, attachment and link recovery, OCR/vision fallback, natural-language classification, receipt pairing, local archival, human-review routing, and Excel output, with diagrams and a concrete directory example.
reviews.concern: The DSH-specific interaction is brief, first setup downloads substantial local dependencies, and macOS support is Apple Silicon with an unsigned, unnotarized build.

reviews.evidence: Ships a local-file video content workbench spanning topic/script creation, Screen Studio binding, subtitles, covers, publishing drafts, analytics sync, long-task tracking, and reusable script rules; README supplies executable prompt workflows and a concrete artifact tree.
reviews.concern: Several major stages depend on separately installed services or skills, some macOS-only, and final recording, editing, publishing, and exception review remain manual by design.

reviews.evidence: Comprehensively documents shipped persistent multi-model teams, bounded DAG planning, per-member routes/tools, foreground and background runs, quality repair loops, retries, token coverage, versioned recipes, backups, Run Center, exports, and multiple UI demonstrations.
reviews.concern: The feature surface is operationally complex, Web-profile-only, and tied to pre-stable DSH versions; provider token coverage and hard budget enforcement have explicit limitations.

reviews.evidence: Ships composable execution/plan, reasoning, review, and evolution controls; isolated evidence-based learning proposals; manual approval and backups; detailed command usage; and explicit combinations for daily work, delivery, high-risk review, and preference learning.
reviews.concern: Current releases are tightly pinned to individual DSH release candidates, and review modes add model latency without running project tests, lint, or builds.

reviews.evidence: README describes a shipped Windows trading application with four-model parallel trading, market and financial data, live account execution, monitoring, risk controls, DingTalk chat, batch and conditional orders, cancellation, and remote app launch commands.
reviews.concern: The main application is commercial closed source, dashboard links are presented as badges rather than embedded demonstrations, and the README provides no tests or substantive validation, security, or failure controls commensurate with autonomous live trading.

reviews.evidence: Ships multi-provider balances and quota windows, provider-reported token aggregation, historical cost and budgets, drilldowns, session analytics, safe CSV/JSON exports, adaptive refresh, many adapters, and a constrained declarative monitor, with a UI preview and precise output contracts.
reviews.concern: Most advanced provider support requires substantial configuration, several upstream account endpoints are unstable or non-public, and the README notes dependence on pre-release Harness interfaces.
